title: A matching transcript isn't an audible clip
statement: Check every generated voice clip against its script and measure how loud its first word is, because a matching transcript doesn't show the clip can be heard.
example: In one lesson every transcript of 55 clips matched, yet 13 clips had a first word 25 to 74 dB below the clip's own mean.
detail: The reading course's checklist blocks any new or re-cut clip that has not passed a listen check: a speech-to-text transcript compared with the script, and the loudness of the first word against the clip's own mean (`grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`, line 84). In one round it caught a take that dropped a clause and a re-cut that turned a bare word into another form, and both were made again (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/ROUND-RESULT.md`, line 21). Across 55 clips of one lesson every transcript matched, yet 13 clips had a first word 25-74 dB below the clip's own mean, all confirmed by an independent RMS measurement, and an earlier first word heard as a different word was the incident that started the check (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/readiness-l5-2026-09-17/sim-review/lens-listen-qa.md`, lines 218-220).
against: The transcriber can mishear too: one word came back as a longer form in both an old and a new take and was left for a person's ear (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/ROUND-RESULT.md`, line 21). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/authoring/peter-pan/fill/l5-l7-parity/batch-2026-09-18/DECISIONS.md`).

evidence.quote: L6 p15 first take dropped "then she would have to find another way"
recut #1 inflected the bare stem "Enchant." → "enchanting"; caught by listen
55 clips checked. 13 onset findings, all confirmed real by independent RMS measurement. 0 transcript mismatches
the first word's attack in the 60ms after that silence falls 25–74dB below the clip's own mean

- 21.09 listen pass (whisper base, all clips) L5: 0 transcript findings; 21 WEAK ATTACK = probe artifact (clips open with 190–350 ms silence; the probe measures 0–60 ms). Follow-up for a quiet session: `scripts/verify/listen-clips.mjs` onset window should start at the first non-silent sample.

The only findings are 9 WEAK ATTACK on L4, which are the known probe artifact: flagged and passed clips have indistinguishable leading silence (0.243-0.292 s), so the probe's 0-60 ms window is measuring encoder silence.
one gentle trim after levelling: low threshold so soft word endings ("Moor", "then") survive,
80 ms pad -> edge silence well under 120 ms. (A 0.012 threshold here clipped final words.)
x = trim(x, thr=0.004, pad=0.08)

Whisper mis-hearings happen (proper nouns, invented names): a transcript finding on "Anansi"/"Iktomi" words is usually whisper, not the clip. Onset findings are far more reliable. The probe now folds these itself (rulings, each tested against the 3 historical true-positives before adoption)
hyphen fold; homophone -i/-y fold (Merci≡mercy) … betrayal→"trail", wendy→"when he" still fail.
5 of 6 findings on the first full G5 pass were probe artifacts, 1 was real.
Whisper is useless on isolated syllables; the generator's read-backs (WORD_PROMPT / CLIP_PROMPT / PROBE) and a human ear are the instruments.
Listen-check every new clip : false PROHIBITED_CONTENT refusals must be rephrased and retried (never ship silence); watch for elision
Required full sound-on page-by-page listening remains open: missing/silent clips, misreads, pacing, highlight drift and unwanted continuation.
They passed the word-for-word read-back but failed the pitch check; the paths are in handover §3.2.

It shipped: rewriting three passages left all four passage clips reading the previous draft.
Whisper heard the first word and matched the text in all four clips; the onset meter flagged a soft attack on L7's bad and line-2 feedback clips, so those two still need a human ear before merge.
Compare the actual speech with the exact script, not just a successful API response.
Proven 2026-09-03: a reviewer heard "betrayal" as "trail" — the /b/ onset sat at -84dB in the vocab card clip — and everything text-side passed.
